rot.doubledPawns.ideia.samisch.e1: Attack: doubled pawns are two pawns of the same colour on the same file. They are born from a recapture: the capturing pawn leaves its file and lands on the file of another pawn.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.samisch.e2: This is the Nimzo-Indian Defence, Sämisch Variation. White has just pushed the pawn to a3, which attacks the bishop on b4, and Black decides whether to trade the bishop for the knight on c3.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.samisch.l1: The bishop captures the knight on c3 with check. Black trades the bishop for the knight to double White's pawns.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.samisch.l2: The pawn on b2 recaptures and moves to the c-file. Now White has doubled pawns on c3 and c4.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.samisch.l3: The weakness: the pawn on c4 has no neighbouring pawn to defend it, and the one on c3 cannot defend it. Black can attack it with the bishop via a6 and the knight via a5.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.samisch.l4: What White gets in return: the b-file without a white pawn, open for the rook, and the pawn on c3, which supports the one on d4 and the advance of the e-pawn to e4.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.samisch.l5: That is why this trade is neither good nor bad in itself, and masters play both sides. Before doubling your opponent's pawns, weigh the weakness against what he gets: the position decides.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.e1: Attack: in a pawn ending, with no other pieces on the board, the weakness of doubled pawns is exposed to the king.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.e2: This position comes from a game played on Lichess. Black has doubled pawns on f6 and f5. The pawn on f6 does not defend the one on f5, and only the black king protects it.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.p: Find the king move that attacks the pawns on f5 and e4.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.certo: The king goes to f4 and attacks f5 and e4 at the same time. The pawn on f6, stuck behind the one on f5, cannot help.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.revela: The king goes to f4: from there it attacks f5 and e4, and the pawn on f6, stuck behind the one on f5, cannot help.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.err.g3: The pawn advances to g4 and offers a trade to the pawn on f5.
With this move Black has a resource: the pawn on f5 captures on g4, and the black pawns are no longer doubled.
Back to the position: look for the king move that attacks the pawns on f5 and e4.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.err.e3: On d4 the king attacks only the pawn on e4, which the one on f5 defends, and from there it cannot reach the one on f5.
Back to the position: look for the square from which the king attacks f5 and e4 at the same time.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.fora: That move does not attack the black pawns. Look for a square next to the white king from which it reaches f5 and e4.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.volta: Try again: look for the king move.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.l1: Black cannot defend both pawns: the one on e4 has only the pawn on f5 as a defender, and the one on f5 has only the king.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.l3: The black king goes to d5 to defend the pawn on e4, but leaves the one on f5 undefended.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.l4: The king captures the pawn on f5, and the pawn on f6 is within reach of the white king.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.finalPeoes.l5: In pawn endings like this one, the front doubled pawn has no pawn to defend it, and the rear one is stuck. Check in the position whether the enemy king can reach them.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: now let us think from Black's side. This position comes from a game played on Lichess. White has doubled pawns on g5 and g2.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra.2: The rook captures the pawn on g5 with check. The pawn on g2 is on the same file and does not defend it, and the pawn on h6 stops the king from recapturing.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra.3: The king steps out of check to f3 and keeps defending the rook on g3.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra.4: The rook captures the rook on g3 with check: Black trades the rooks.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra.5: The king recaptures. What is left is a pawn ending in which Black has two pawns against one.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra.6: In endings like this one, the front doubled pawn falls easily, because the rear one does not defend it. Here it fell, and the trade of rooks left Black a pawn up.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: back to White. This position also comes from a Lichess game. Black has doubled pawns on g6 and g4, and the black king stands between the rook on d6 and the pawn on g6.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra2.2: The rook captures the pawn on g6 with check. The pawn on g4 does not defend it, and the king on e6 blocks the defence of the rook on d6.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra2.3: The king steps out of check to e5. Any king square leaves the rook on d6 attacked by the rook on g6.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra2.4: The rook captures the rook on d6, and White trades the rooks.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra2.5: The king recaptures on d6. Now the other doubled pawn, the one on g4, is on its own.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra2.6: The pawn on h3 captures the one on g4. Both doubled pawns have fallen, and White is left with three pawns against two.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.regra2.7: The doubled pawn on g6 fell with check, because the one on g4 did not defend it. The one on g4, alone on the file, fell afterwards.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.e1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, who has the doubled pawns. This position comes from a Berlin Defence of the Ruy Lopez played on Lichess. Black has doubled pawns on c7 and c6, and on f7 and f6.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.e2: The pawn that went to f6 left the g-file without a black pawn. The rook on g8 and the queen on g6 stand on that file, facing the white king on g1.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.p: Find the move that uses the g-file against the white king.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.certo: The queen captures the pawn on g3 with check. The pawn on f2 cannot recapture, because the bishop on c5 pins it to the king.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.revela: The queen captures the pawn on g3 with check. The pawn on f2 cannot recapture, because the bishop on c5 pins it to the king.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.err.g6e4.1: The queen captures the pawn on e4, but leaves the g-file, and the attack on the white king is over.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.err.g6e4.2: Back to the position: look for the move that uses the g-file against the white king.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.err.g6g4.1: On g4 the queen is attacked by the pawn on h3, which captures it.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.err.g6g4.2: Back to the position: look for a check along the g-file.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.err.g6h6.1: On h6 the queen leaves the g-file, and the check on g3 is gone.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.err.g6h6.2: Back to the position: keep the queen on the g-file and look for the check.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.fora: That move does not use the g-file. Look for a queen or rook move along it.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.l0: The check comes along the g-file, which the recapture on f6 left without a black pawn.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.l1: The king has only h1 to step out of check.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.l2: The queen gives mate on g2, defended by the rook on g8 along the g-file.
rot.doubledPawns.ideia.coluna.l3: Here the doubled pawns came with the g-file open to attack the king. Before judging your doubled pawns as a weakness, see what the recapture gave in return.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: back to White, who now has the doubled pawns on f2 and f3. The g-file has no white pawn, and both white rooks stand on it, facing the black king on g8.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.excecao.2: The rook captures the pawn on g7 with check, defended by the other rook along the g-file.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.excecao.3: The king has only h8 to step out of check.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.excecao.4: The rook goes to h7, defended by the bishop on d3, and it is mate: the rook on g1 takes g8 away from the king.
rot.doubledPawns.demos.excecao.5: Again, the doubled pawns gave an open file against the king, and it was worth more than the weakness of the pawns.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.valeAqui.enunci: Your pawns on f2 and f3 are doubled. Are they only a weakness here, or did they give something in return? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The doubled pawns left the g-file without a white pawn. The bishop checked on g7, the rook took it, and the queen took the rook with mate.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.valeAqui.err.g2: The queen on g7 is captured by the rook on g8, and the attack loses its force. Look for a check that lures the rook from g8 to g7, where the queen can capture it.
The queen leaves the g-file, and the attack on the black king is over. Look for a check that lures the rook from g8 to g7.
With the queen on f1, the rook on g8 trades itself for the one on g1, and the attack along the g-file is over. Look for a check that lures the rook from g8 to g7.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.torres.enunciad: Now let us think from Black's side. White's pawns on f2 and f3 are doubled. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.torres.fim: The pawn on f3 fell with check: the one on f2 did not defend it, and the rook on d3 stopped the king from recapturing.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.torres.err.d3f3: With the rook from d3 on f3, the rook on a3 recaptures on f3, and Black is a rook down. Capture with the rook on f7.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.torres.err.d3a3: With the trade of rooks, the white king is free to defend the pawn on f3, and Black loses the advantage. Capture the pawn on f3 while the rook on d3 stops the king from recapturing.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.torres.err.d3d7: The rook on d3 retreats, and the white king is free to defend the pawn on f3. Capture it now, while the rook on d3 stops the king from recapturing.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.torres.err2: Both black rooks are attacked: the one on d3 by the rook on a3, and the one on f3 by the king. Capture the rook on a3.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.reiNoFinal.enun: Back to White, in a pawn ending. Black's pawns on h7 and h5 are doubled. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.reiNoFinal.fim: The king went to h4 and captured the pawn on h5: the one on h7, behind it, could not defend it.
On h3 the king does not yet attack the pawn on h5. Look for the square from which it reaches it.
The f-pawn advance attacks no black pawn. Your king has a path to the front doubled pawn.
The f-pawn advance to f4 attacks no black pawn and gives the black king time to reach g6. Your king has a path to the front doubled pawn.
rot.doubledPawns.pratica.reiNoFinal.err2: The f-pawn advance wastes a tempo: the black king reaches g7 and defends the pawn on h7. The pawn on h5 is within your king's reach now.
